'''Narayan S. Hosmane''' (born 30 June 1948) is an [[India|Indian-born]] [[cancer research]] scientist and a distinguished research professor of Chemistry and [[Biochemistry]]. He was featured in NRI Achievers magazine.<ref name="nriachievers">{{cite web|url=http://www.nriachievers.org/prev_magzine_index.html|title=The Wizard & His Inspiring Life Story: Narayan S. Hosmane|access-date=2008-06-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080626061246/http://www.nriachievers.org/prev_magzine_index.html|archive-date=2008-06-26|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is a two-time recipient of the [[Humboldt Research Award]] for senior scientists, an annual award presented by the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]], [[Bonn]], [[Germany]], to scientists worldwide in recognition of their career accomplishments.<ref name="Humboldt2">{{cite web|url=http://www.niu.edu/PubAffairs/RELEASES/2007/aug/hosmane.shtml|title=NIU news release&nbsp;– NIU's Narayan Hosmane|access-date=2008-06-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080706162825/http://www.niu.edu/PubAffairs/RELEASES/2007/aug/hosmane.shtml|archive-date=2008-07-06|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He founded "Boron in the Americas" (formerly known as BUSA) and hosted the organization's first meeting in [[Dallas]] in April 1988.<ref name="backgroundinfo">{{cite web|url=http://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f9/Background_Info.hosmane.08.pdf|title=Prof. Narayan S. Hosmane Background Information}}{{dead link|date=February 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> He has published over 300 papers in scientific journals and was ranked by the [[Institute for Scientific Information]] (ISI) in the top 50% of the most cited chemists in the world from 1981–1997.<ref name="backgroundinfo" /> He is a fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] and the [[American Institute of Chemists]], a foreign member of Russian Academy of Natural Sciences (RANS),<ref name="niu.edu">{{cite web|url=http://www.niutoday.info/2013/06/11/niu-chemistry-professor-narayan-hosmane-elected-to-russian-academy-of-natural-sciences|title=Foreign Member of the Russian Academy of Natural Sciences}}</ref> and listed in [[Who's Who in the World]].<ref name="backgroundinfo" />

==Early life==
Hosmane was born in [[Karnataka, India|Gokarna]], [[Uttar Kannada]] district, India, in 1948,<ref name="backgroundinfo" /> to a [[Havyaka]] [[Brahmin]] family. He earned his high school diploma from [[Bhadrakali High School, Gokarna]] in 1964, and attended [[Dr. A. V. Baliga college, Kumta]], where he earned his [[Bachelor of Science]] in Chemistry with Botany as a minor.

He is married to Sumathy Rao, who is from a [[Konkani language|Konkani]]-speaking family. They have a daughter and a son.

== Academic career ==
Hosmane earned a [[Master of Science]] degree from [[Karnataka University]], India.<ref name="nriachievers" /> He obtained a [[Ph.D.]] degree in [[Organometallic]]/[[Inorganic Chemistry]] in 1974 from the [[University of Edinburgh]], Scotland, with a dissertation titled 'Some reactions of stannic chloride with silicon hydrides and some novel group IV derivatives of mercury.'<ref>{{Cite journal|last=S.|first=Hosmane, Narayan|date=1974|title=Some reactions of stannic chloride with silicon hydrides and some novel group IV derivatives of mercury|hdl=1842/14102|url=https://www.era.lib.ed.ac.uk/handle/1842/14102|language=en}}</ref>

After postdoctoral research at [[Queen's University Belfast]], he joined the Lambeg Industrial Research Institute in [[Northern Ireland]], and then moved to the United States to study [[carboranes]] and metallacarboranes.<ref name="backgroundinfo" /> After postdoctoral work with Russell Grimes at the [[University of Virginia]], he joined the faculty at the [[Virginia Polytechnic Institute]] and State University in 1979.<br /> In 1982, he joined the faculty at [[Southern Methodist University]], where he became Professor of Chemistry in 1989. In 1998, he moved to [[Northern Illinois University]] and is currently a Distinguished Research Professor of Chemistry and Biochemistry and the Inaugural Board of Trustees Professor.<ref name="nriachievers" />

In 2011, while attempting to produce [[carbon nanotube|single-walled carbon nanotubes]], Hosmane discovered that a known technique for carbon production (burning magnesium with dry ice) produced layers of [[graphene]].<ref name="Gizmag">{{cite web |last1=Coxworth |first1=Ben |date=21 June 2011 |title='Simple, green, and cost-effective' method of graphene production announced |url=http://www.gizmag.com/graphene-production-magnesium-dry-ice/18986/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150522104032/http://www.gizmag.com/graphene-production-magnesium-dry-ice/18986/ |archive-date=2015-05-22 |accessdate=7 June 2015 |publisher=Gizmag}}</ref>

== Professional affiliations ==
* Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (CChem FRSC)<ref name="personalpage" />
* Fellow of the [[American Institute of Chemists]] (FAIC)
* Member of the [[American Chemical Society]] (ACS)
* Member of the [[Sigma Xi]] Society
* Member of the [[International Council on Main Group Chemistry, Inc.]] (ICMGC)

== Boards and editorships ==
[[File:Hosmane pravasi2-1-.jpg|thumb|Prof. Dr. Narayan S. Hosmane receiving "Lifetime Achievement Pravasi Award"]] 
* Section Editor of ''[[Applied Organometallic Chemistry]]'', 2003–present<ref name="personalpage" />
* International Editorial Advisory Board for [[Organometallics]], a journal of the American Chemical Society, Jan 2006–present
* Regional Editor of ''[[Molecules (journal)|Molecules]]'', an international Internet journal.
* Editorial boards, ''[[Main Group Metal Chemistry]]'' (1999 – present) and ''[[Main Group Chemistry]]'' (2006 – present)
* Guest Editor, Special Issue of the ''[[Applied Organometallic Chemistry]]'' – Main Group Metal Compounds commemorating 65th birthday of Professor Thomas P. Fehlner entitled "Recent Advances in Inorganometallic Chemistry" published by Wiley-VCH, in April / May 2003.&nbsp;
* Guest Editor, Special Issue of the ''[[Journal of Organometallic Chemistry]]'' commemorating 70th birthday of Professor Sheldon G. Shore entitled "From Borane Cages to Metal Clusters: Recent Developments," published by Elsevier Science, in November 2000.
* Guest Editor, Special Issue of ''[[Phosphorus, Sulfur, and Silicon]]'' Volume 87, Numbers 1–4, 1994) entitled "Symposium on Recent Advances in the Chemistry of the Main-Group Elements," Austin, Texas, 24–27 October 1993, published by Gordon and Breach.
